bib.title: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Language Models
bib.venue: Transactions on Machine Learning Research (05/2024); arXiv v5

question: Can a sub-1B model be fine-tuned to produce useful chain-of-thought rationales from text plus images, and does separating rationale generation from answer inference help?
hypothesis: Hallucinated rationales mislead small models; giving rationale generation vision features yields better rationales and better answers.
contributions: First study of CoT reasoning in different modalities in peer-reviewed literature
Two-stage framework fine-tuning LMs to fuse vision and language representations
Analysis of why naive CoT fails and how vision features alleviate it, general across tasks and backbones

method.summary: Two T5 models of identical architecture are fine-tuned independently: stage 1 generates a rationale from question/context/options plus ViT patch features; stage 2 appends the rationale to the text input and predicts the answer. Vision features are fused after the text encoder by single-head attention and gated fusion.
method.task: multimodal multiple-choice science QA with rationales

datasets.name: ScienceQA
datasets.preprocessing: InstructBLIP image captions appended to context; all-zero vectors for questions without an image

datasets.name: A-OKVQA
datasets.split: train/val/test; evaluated on validation as test is hidden; multiple-choice setting

models.name: Multimodal-CoT Base
models.architecture: T5 encoder-decoder + frozen ViT-large features + gated fusion

models.name: GPT-3.5, ChatGPT, GPT-4, Chameleon, LLaMA-Adapter, LLaVA, InstructBLIP, VQA models, UnifiedQA

training.objective: supervised next-token loss on X->R (stage 1) and XR->A (stage 2), trained independently

inference.prompting: fine-tuned, no prompts; LLM baselines use 2 in-context examples from training set (as Lu et al. 2022a)

other.input_format: Q, C, M concatenated; stage 2 appends rationale

eval.protocol: single reported numbers, no seeds or significance tests stated; error analysis by manual inspection of 50 cases

prompts.purpose: zero-shot rationale generation by InstructBLIP/ChatGPT for pseudo-rationales
prompts.text:
Please explain the rationale to choose the correct answer.
Solution:

results.quote: achieves substantial performance gains over the prior best model in publications (86.54%→90.45%)

results.claim: Multimodal-CoT Base (223M) reaches 85.31% average on ScienceQA

results.quote: we observe a ↓12.31% accuracy decrease (81.63%→69.32%) if the model predicts rationales before answers (QCM→RA)

results.claim: Explanation format (answer then rationale, QCM->AR) scores 69.68
Two-stage text-only baseline gets RougeL 90.73 for rationales but only 78.57% answer accuracy, below the no-CoT 81.63%

results.quote: the answer inference accuracy is only 78.57%

results.claim: Captions as image substitute add only 0.80 points (78.57 to 79.37)
